publisher: Mammalian Genome (Springer), via Europe PMC; Gandolfi B, Outerbridge CA, Beresford LG, Myers JA, Pimentel M, Alhaddad H, Grahn JC, Grahn RA, Lyons LA. 2010
pageTitle: The naked truth: Sphynx and Devon Rex cat breed mutations in KRT71.
quote: A SNP altering a splice site was identified in the Sphynx breed and suggested to be the hairless (hr) allele, and a complex sequence alteration, also causing a splice variation, was identified in the Devon Rex breed and suggested to be the curly (re) allele. ... All the Devon Rex were homozygous for the complex alterations and most of the Sphynx were either homozygous for the hr allele or compound heterozygotes with the Devon-associated re allele
newFact: A hairless Sphynx and a curly Devon Rex look like total opposites, but their coats come down to the same gene. In 2010, scientists traced the Sphynx's naked look and the Devon Rex's curls to two different mutations in one keratin gene, KRT71. Some Sphynx even carry one copy of each version!
note: Lead angle sourced. The paper's real title is 'The naked truth: Sphynx and Devon Rex cat breed mutations in KRT71' (PMID 20953787, PMC2974189, doi 10.1007/s00335-010-9290-6), not 'To the root of the curl'. Quote is from the abstract; plain-text copy at cache/krt71-naked-truth-abstract.txt. 'Some Sphynx carry one copy of each' rests on 'compound heterozygotes with the Devon-associated re allele'. Photo (Sphynx on a sunny blanket) still fits; no whiskers, no care advice. 1 fetch used.
